rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12, AB 1482)
rules.requirement: Over any 12-month period an owner may not raise gross rent by more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. No more than two increases are allowed per 12 months. Waivers are void. Tenants may sue for injunctive relief, excess rent, attorney's fees and up to treble damages for willful violations; the AG and city attorneys may also enforce.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10% per 12 months; max 2 increases
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property in California, including mobilehome park units, except housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (rolling) and other listed exemptions. Does not apply where stricter local rent control applies.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school dormitories; units under stricter local rent control; CofO within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units (single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, if the statutory written exemption notice was given; owner-occupied duplexes where the owner lived in one unit at the start of the tenancy (neither unit an ADU/JADU); mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption notice for separately alienable units; owner entity type; owner occupancy of a duplex; affordable-housing deed restrictions or subsidy; dormitory status; whether stricter local rent control applies.

rules.conflict_note: AB 1482 took effect 2020-01-01 (per LAHD page) and covers increases on or after March 15, 2019. Current text was re-added by SB 567 (Stats. 2023, ch. 290), operative 2024-04-01. Repealed as of 2030-01-01. Yields to stricter local rent control (Berkeley, SF, LA RSO, Santa Ana) where those apply.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction (Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied for 12 months (24 months if adult tenants were added), the owner may terminate only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written notice. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay relocation assistance of one month's rent within 15 days, or waive the final month's rent. Noncompliant notices are void. Violators face actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to treble plus punitive damages for willful violations.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months' occupancy; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including mobilehome park units, after 12 months of occupancy. Does not apply where a qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospitals and care facilities; dormitories; tenant shares bath or kitchen with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family home renting no more than two units or bedrooms (incl. ADU/JADU); owner-occupied duplexes; CofO within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, with the required notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners; units under a qualifying local just cause ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant occupancy duration (12/24 months); owner entity type and exemption notice; owner occupancy or shared facilities; affordable-housing restrictions; whether a local just cause ordinance applies.

rules.conflict_note: Original AB 1482 protections date to 2020. The current version was operative 2024-04-01 and amended by AB 1529, effective 2026-01-01. Repealed 2030-01-01. Does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or a more protective later ordinance, applies.

rules.title: California security deposit law: one-month cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
rules.requirement: Security, however labeled, is capped at one month's rent in addition to first month's rent, for security collected on or after July 1, 2024. Small natural-person landlords (no more than two properties and four units total) may charge up to two months, but not to service members. Higher-than-standard security charged to a service member must be explained in writing and the excess returned within 6 months. Security may not be called nonrefundable. The landlord must offer a pre-move-out walk-through in the last two weeks of the tenancy. Within 21 days of move-out, the landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement, receipts and invoices (if deductions exceed $125), and proof that repairs were done (from 2025-01-01). Move-out photos are required from 2025-04-01, and move-in photos for tenancies starting on or after 2025-07-01. If paid electronically, the deposit must be returned electronically (from 2026-01-01). Bad-faith retention carries up to twice the deposit in statutory damages.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords); 21-day return
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental agreements in California for security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024.
rules.exemptions: Small landlord exception: a natural person, family trust, or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total may charge two months (not available for service-member tenants). Advance payment of six or more months' rent on a lease of six months or longer.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Small-landlord exception depends on the owner's whole portfolio and ownership form; service-member status; collection date; electronic payment.

rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (as amended by AB 12, 2023, and AB 414, 2025)
rules.conflict_note: Different provisions take effect on different dates: cap 2024-07-01; service-member and move-out photo rules 2025-04-01; move-in photos for tenancies starting on or after 2025-07-01; electronic return 2026-01-01 (AB 414).

rules.title: California application screening fee cap and procedures (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A screening fee may not exceed actual out-of-pocket costs plus reasonable time, and never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998 (reported as $68.96 for 2026). No fee may be charged if no unit is or will reasonably be available. A fee may be collected only if the landlord offers either (a) first-come consideration under written criteria, or (b) a refund to applicants not selected within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, return any unused portion, and provide a copy of the credit report within 7 days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: $30 CPI-adjusted (≈$68.96 in 2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, a screening fee.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt fee rules under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.conflict_note: The $30 base cap dates to the 1990s. The current text was amended by AB 1170 (Stats. 2025, ch. 67), effective 2026-01-01; the first-come/refund requirement in (c)(2) appears to come from that amendment. The $68.96 2026 figure is from the Berkeley Rent Board.

rules.title: FEHA housing discrimination including source of income and subsidy screening limits (Gov. Code § 12955)
rules.requirement: Housing owners may not discriminate in screening or renting based on protected characteristics, including source of income. This includes Section 8 and other vouchers since SB 329 (2020-01-01), so 'No Section 8' policies are barred. Income standards must be based on the tenant's portion of rent where there is a government subsidy, and must count the aggregate income of co-residents. Since SB 267 (2024-01-01), credit history may not be used for subsidized applicants unless they are offered the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay. Owners also may not charge higher deposits based on protected characteristics, or pet deposits or pet rent for assistance animals.
rules.key_value: Source-of-income protection incl. vouchers; alternative evidence required instead of credit for subsidized applicants
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations in California, landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person (discriminatory advertising still barred); limited shared-living, senior housing and homeless-youth exceptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption; subsidy-specific provisions apply only to applicants with government rent subsidies.

rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (FEHA), as amended by SB 329 (2019) and SB 267 (2023)
rules.conflict_note: Original effective date not stated. Source-of-income coverage of vouchers dates from 2020-01-01; the SB 267 credit-history rule from 2024-01-01.

rules.title: Civil Rights Council regulations limiting criminal history in housing decisions
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not use blanket bans on people with criminal histories. Denials based on a conviction must be directly related to suitability for tenancy and individually assessed.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; no arrest-only, sealed/expunged or juvenile records
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers, landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies in California.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption.

rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council FEHA regulations on criminal history in housing (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 2; section not stated in corpus)
rules.conflict_note: Regulation section numbers are not given. The effective date comes from the CAA secondary source.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms in restraint of trade or with coercion (AB 325)
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (one used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set prices or terms) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. Applies generally, including to rental housing. Remedies include criminal fines, civil fines up to $1M per violation, and treble damages in private suits.
rules.key_value: Ban on common pricing algorithm in a conspiracy or with coercion
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person other than an end consumer that uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm in California, including landlords and rental pricing vendors.
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade, or with coercion.

rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.conflict_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06. The 2026-01-01 effective date is the default regular-session date, confirmed by a secondary source. This is a general antitrust statute; local bans (SF, Berkeley, San Diego, Santa Ana) apply alongside it.

rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (one using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Vendors may not sell, license or provide such algorithms to Berkeley landlords. The City Attorney and tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and each unit a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Ban; up to $1,000 per violation per unit per month
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords of residential units in Berkeley and vendors of coordinated pricing algorithms.
rules.exemptions: Aggregated anonymous data products that do not recommend rents; affordable-housing rent or income-limit tools; market research for financing or appraisal, and software R&D (if competitor data is not an input to recommendations).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a coordinated pricing algorithm using nonpublic competitor data is used.

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63, as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.conflict_note: Sources disagree on timing. The official document shows only that amending Ord. 7,992-N.S. was passed to print 2025-11-18, with second reading 2025-12-02, and states no effective date; the original Chapter 13.63 predates it. Morgan Lewis gives January 2026. RealPage v. City of Berkeley was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-01-14.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC ch. 13.106)
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, terminating, or charging a higher deposit or rent based on criminal history. Penalties: administrative fines of $1,000-$10,000 per violation, damages (actual or three times monthly rent), punitive damages, fees and injunctions.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiry and use banned
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing in Berkeley, covering advertising, applications, leasing, tenancy and family-member additions.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex-offender registrants; limited public housing and Section 8 exemptions; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties where an owner of record lives as primary residence; owner move-back agreements under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; subsidized-housing status; move-back agreements.

rules.conflict_note: Passed 2020-04-14; effective date not stated.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization rent ceilings and Annual General Adjustment (BMC 13.76)
rules.requirement: For fully covered units, rent ceilings may rise each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (65% of Bay Area CPI change), capped at 5% by Measure BB. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, effective no earlier than 2026-01-01, for eligible landlords (Reg. 1148) who give notice. Banked AGAs may be used to reach the ceiling. Capital improvement petitions are allowed only for completed work. For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06, utilities must be in base rent unless separately metered in the tenant's name. Government-subsidized units are now fully or partially covered.
rules.key_value: AGA 1.0% for 2026; max 5%
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most multifamily units with a CofO before July 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses with 5+ individually rented rooms; covered subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: No rent ceiling for new construction with CofO after June 1980, single-family homes with tenancies from 1996 on, most condos, Section 202/811 units and HUD-mortgage project-based units, or tenancies from 2025 with Costa-Hawkins-set rents (for the 2026 AGA). Fully exempt: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied since 12/31/1979); shared kitchen/bath with owner; post-11/7/2018 tenancies on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit co-ops.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy start date (single-family before 1996; Costa-Hawkins); condo status; owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared facilities, ADU); subsidy type; landlord registration eligibility (Reg. 1148).

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.76.110A; Rent Board Reg. 1148; Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.conflict_note: Sources describe the cutoff both as 'built before 1980' and as 'CofO after June 1980'; the June 1980 CofO cutoff is used here. Measure BB's effective date is not stated, and its 2024-02-06 utility applicability date predates the election. Where Berkeley rent ceilings apply, state § 1947.12 yields.

rules.title: Berkeley just cause for eviction (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Under Measure BB: no nonpayment eviction for debt under one month's HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont); no eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease; lease-breach evictions require a material term, actual harm and unreasonable conduct. Notices must cite Rent Board counseling resources, and copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summonses must be filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days. Owner move-in evictions require relocation assistance, indexed annually: $19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households, effective 2026-01-01.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; OMI relocation $19,413 (+$6,471 qualifying) for 2026
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units, including post-1980 new construction, single-family homes, most condos and subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex; tenant shares kitchen or bath with an owner present at the start of the tenancy; post-11/7/2018 tenancies on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit co-ops.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared facilities, ADU); tenancy start date; university or co-op status.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (BMC ch. 13.76), as amended by Measure BB
rules.conflict_note: No code section or original effective date is given in the corpus. Relocation amounts are the 2026 adjustment adopted 2025-10-16. State § 1946.2 yields where this ordinance applies.

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Owners evicting tenants to withdraw property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions: $19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households for 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: Berkeley tenants evicted for Ellis Act withdrawal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to Ellis Act withdrawals; qualifying-household criteria are not stated.

rules.conflict_note: Amounts took effect 2026-01-01 (adopted 2025-10-16). The original ordinance date and code section are not given.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, with a prorated amount if the tenant moves out mid-year.
rules.key_value: Annual interest; prorated at move-out
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex; shared kitchen/bath with owner; owner-occupied ADU properties (post-11/7/2018 tenancies); dormitories; nonprofit co-ops.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy exemptions; rate not stated.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance
rules.conflict_note: Interest rate and code section are not stated in the corpus.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable renewal fees (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement: Owners charging an application or credit-report fee must give a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement before receiving the fee, and must state the maximum fee allowed under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). Owners may not charge existing tenants non-refundable fees to renew a tenancy, including fees for roommate departure, addition or replacement. Contrary lease terms are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners and agents of residential rental property in Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: The URL required in the rights statement was still to be provided by the City.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic devices to set rents or occupancy (Admin. Code § 37.10C)
rules.requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or manage occupancy for San Francisco residential units is prohibited. Tenants and the City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month per affected unit may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per unit-month
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and vendors with respect to residential units in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a device using nonpublic competitor data is used.

rules.conflict_note: Approved by the Board of Supervisors July 2024; effective 2024-10-14 per sf.gov. Now at issue in Gomez v. Greystar (N.D. Cal.).

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction and relocation (§§ 37.9, 37.9A, 37.9C)
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict from covered units only for one of 17 enumerated just causes, and that cause must be the dominant motive. Lease expiration or a change of ownership is not just cause. For owner/relative move-in, demolition or removal, temporary capital improvement, or substantial rehabilitation (notices served 3/1/26-2/28/27), relocation is $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly, disabled or minor-child household. Ellis Act relocation is $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Temporary capital improvement displacement under 20 days is governed by Civ. Code § 1947.9 ($446/day plus moving expenses).
rules.key_value: 17 just causes; relocation $8,245/tenant (Ellis $11,110.05) for 3/1/26-2/28/27
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions, including units exempt from rent limits such as post-6/13/1979 new construction and Costa-Hawkins units.
rules.exemptions: Units not covered by the Rent Ordinance (specific exemptions not listed in the corpus).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Eviction ground and notice date determine relocation; some government-regulated tenancies vary.

rules.conflict_note: Relocation amounts are indexed annually. State § 1946.2 yields where this ordinance applies.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable increase
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, annual increases are limited to the Rent Board's allowable amount: 1.6% of base rent for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units under the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. Units with a CofO first issued after June 13, 1979 are exempt from rent increase limits.
rules.exemptions: New construction with a CofO after June 13, 1979; Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies; some government-regulated rents.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins exemption (single-family/condo) and government-regulated rent status.

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Ordinance (S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37); Rent Board annual increase announcement
rules.conflict_note: The rate is reset annually: 1.4% in 2025-26, 1.6% through 2027-02-28. The June 13, 1979 cutoff comes from the sf.gov just cause page. State § 1947.12 yields where local rent control applies.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security deposits held by San Francisco residential landlords.
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board Security Deposit Interest Rates (Form 572)
rules.conflict_note: No ordinance section is given. Prior rates were 5.0% (2025-26) and 5.2% (2024-25).

rules.title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: Protects applicants and residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions in San Francisco.
rules.coverage_conditions: Affordable housing in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to affordable housing; qualifying properties are not defined in the source.

rules.conflict_note: Summary-level source; no code citation or detailed limits.

rules.title: San Diego prohibition on algorithmic rent-setting devices (SDMC §§ 98.1101-98.1104)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use an algorithmic device (software analyzing nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy) to set rents or occupancy for residential rental property. No person may sell, license or provide such a device to a landlord. Tenants may sue for injunctive relief, damages and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; attorney's fees are recoverable.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per month per property
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in San Diego and vendors of algorithmic devices.
rules.exemptions: Reports from aggregated nonpublic data more than 90 days old, or from public data, that do not recommend rents; affordable-housing program tools.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where qualifying software is used.

rules.conflict_note: The official city document is a Feb. 2025 draft with a blank passage date (pending in that source). Morgan Lewis (Aug. 2026) and OCBJ report it enacted and in effect from June 2025. Now at issue in Keller v. UDR (S.D. Cal.).

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections Ordinance just cause (SDMC §§ 98.0701-98.0710)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy of more than 30 days without an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause. Curable violations require notice and an opportunity to cure. Owner move-in under leases from 2023-06-24 requires tenant agreement or a lease clause, and substantial remodels require permits. For no-fault terminations, relocation is 2 months' rent (3 months for tenants 62+ or disabled), paid within 15 days or as a rent waiver, plus notice of rights and a right of first offer. Wrongful eviction carries at least 3x damages and voids the notice.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 30 days; no-fault relocation 2 months' rent (3 for seniors/disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego, including mobilehome units, for tenancies over 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less).
rules.exemptions: Hotels and short-term rentals; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); MRL mobilehomes; care facilities; dormitories; shared bath or kitchen with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family homes and duplexes; CofO within previous 15 years; separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC, with notice.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy length; owner entity and exemption notice; owner occupancy; affordable-housing status.

rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.0701-98.0710 (O-21647 N.S., amended O-21769 N.S.)
rules.conflict_note: Amended 2024-03-28 (§ 98.0710 added). Supplements Civ. Code § 1946.2. The Commission notice requirement depends on a portal.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (Ord. NS-3090)
rules.requirement: The sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data to set rents for Santa Ana residential property is prohibited. Tenants need only prove use, not collusion. Remedies are private claims for injunctive relief, damages and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation and per month, plus attorney's fees; code enforcement fines are also available.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in Santa Ana and software vendors.
rules.exemptions: Software relying solely on public or aggregate historical data; affordable housing compliance tools.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where qualifying software is used.

rules.conflict_note: First reading 2026-02-17, final adoption about 2026-03-03, effective 2026-04-02 per Morgan Lewis. The PublicCEO article predates adoption. The Apartment Association raised potential legal challenges.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual cap
rules.requirement: Rent may be raised once a year by no more than the lower of 3% or 80% of the CPI change, and not at all if CPI is negative. The City publishes the allowable increase by June 30, effective September 1. The allowable increase for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027 is 2.87%. Owners may petition for a fair-return increase, and tenants may petition against excess increases.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental buildings constructed on or before February 1, 1995, and mobilehome spaces offered for rent on or before January 1, 1990.
rules.exemptions: Buildings constructed after 2/1/1995; mobilehome spaces offered after 1/1/1990; state-law (Costa-Hawkins) exemptions not detailed.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins exemptions; fair-return petitions.

rules.conflict_note: No code citation is given. State § 1947.12 yields where local rent control applies.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of occupancy, an owner may terminate only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in a written notice, after notice and an opportunity to cure where applicable. No-fault terminations require 3 months' relocation assistance or a waiver of the final 3 months' rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 30 days; 3 months' relocation for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Santa Ana after 30 days of occupancy.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotels and transient occupancy; hospitals and care facilities; dormitories; shared living quarters.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy over 30 days; affordable, transient, care-facility and shared-living exemptions.

rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (2021)
rules.conflict_note: The 15-year exemption basis (construction vs. CofO) is unclear. No code citation is given.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance allowable increase (LAMC Ch. XV)
rules.requirement: Rent for RSO units may be raised once every 12 months, by the LAHD-published allowable percentage (3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026). Registered RSO and SCEP fee surcharges may be passed through with notice. Since 2026-02-02, no additional percentage for utilities and no 10% increase for added dependents are allowed; a 10% increase for an added non-dependent tenant remains, if imposed within 60 days. Rent resets to market on voluntary vacancy or specified at-fault evictions.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months at LAHD allowable % (3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Includes apartments, condos, duplexes, 2+ single-family homes on a parcel, ADUs and mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Rent not regulated for condo or townhome tenancies beginning after 12/31/1995; luxury exemption based on May 1978 rent; temporary exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Replacement units covered regardless of age; condo tenancy start date; luxury exemption.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, LAMC Ch. XV, Art. 1
rules.conflict_note: Allowable-increase formula changed effective 2026-02-02 (utility and dependent add-ons eliminated). The 3% figure covered only through 2026-06-30; the 7/1/2026-6/30/2027 percentage is not in the corpus. The page says 'first built', which may differ from the ordinance's CofO basis. State § 1947.12 yields to the RSO.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO just cause eviction and relocation (LAMC 151.09, 151.30)
rules.requirement: RSO tenants may be evicted only for listed at-fault reasons or listed no-fault reasons (151.09.A). Since 2023-03-27, nonpayment evictions require arrears above one month's Fair Market Rent. For no-fault evictions the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice, file the notice within 3 business days, and pay relocation within 15 days or escrow it. Amounts for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027: Eligible $11,000 or $14,400; Qualified $23,150 or $27,400. Reduced Mom and Pop amounts for owner or relative move-in (151.30) are $10,550 / $21,250. The same filing, FMR and relocation rules apply to JCO units.
rules.key_value: Relocation $11,000-$27,400 (7/1/2026-6/30/2027); FMR nonpayment threshold
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in the City of Los Angeles (generally built on or before October 1, 1978).
rules.exemptions: Relocation not owed when replacing a resident manager or for natural-disaster hazards not caused by the landlord.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Relocation amount depends on tenant age, disability, children, tenure and income; Mom and Pop reduction depends on owner holdings.

rules.conflict_note: Bulletins give 3 days in one place and 3 business days in another for the notice filing. Relocation amounts are adjusted each July 1. State § 1946.2 yields.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (LAMC 165)
rules.requirement: For non-RSO units, landlords may terminate only for listed at-fault or no-fault just causes (LAMC 165.03), once the tenant has lived there 6 months or the original lease has expired. No-fault evictions require a Declaration filing and relocation assistance (165.06). For single-family dwellings owned by qualifying natural persons, relocation is one month's rent. Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days. The FMR nonpayment threshold applies.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 6 months or lease expiry; no-fault relocation
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units in Los Angeles not covered by the RSO, including post-10/1/1978 buildings and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; care facilities; fraternity and sorority houses; owner's roommate; certain co-ops; some nonprofit, homeless and treatment facilities; some government or HACLA properties; RSO units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy at least 6 months or lease expired; not RSO-regulated; facility-type exemptions; owner's-roommate exemption.

rules.conflict_note: LAHD says the JCO 'can apply' to buildings newer than 10/1/1978. It also covers older non-RSO single-family homes, so no strict date cutoff is set. The JCO does not regulate rent; the state cap may apply instead.

rules.title: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance enhanced relocation for demolition
rules.requirement: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must pay lower-income households (at or below 80% AMI) enhanced relocation. Standardized payments for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027: Extremely Low $115,480, Very Low $96,750, Low $87,450, or another approved option. All tenants still receive at least the RSO/JCO amounts within 15 days. Penalties start at $250,000 per displaced unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected Units (all RSO units; units rent-controlled, affordability-restricted or rented to lower-income households within 5 years; units Ellis-withdrawn within 10 years) demolished for new construction.
rules.exemptions: Above-low-income households receive regular RSO/JCO amounts.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Protected Unit status; demolition for new construction; household income.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Ordinance Nos. 188481, 188482; Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6
rules.conflict_note: The state Housing Crisis Act independently requires enhanced relocation.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest (LAMC 151.06.02)
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay interest on security deposits at the City's annually set rate (e.g., 4.320% for 2025), accruing monthly since 1990-11-01. Interest is paid directly or as a rent credit, monthly or yearly, with written notice of the method.
rules.key_value: Annual City-set rate (4.320% for 2025)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Los Angeles RSO.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be RSO-covered.

rules.conflict_note: The 2026 rate is not in the corpus. Detail comes from an AAGLA secondary source.

rules.title: NJ FAIR Act (Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent), P.L.2026, c.43
rules.requirement: Rental property owners and their agents may not pay for or use a coordinator: algorithmic revenue management software or a device that uses competitors' nonpublic, competitively sensitive data to set or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy. No person may perform a coordinating function or engage in parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act, and complaints may be made to the Attorney General.
rules.key_value: Ban on rent coordination software using nonpublic competitor data
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental units in NJ, their agents, and coordinators.
rules.exemptions: Medical, long-term care and correctional facilities; non-AI spreadsheets; free public rent estimates; equal-terms listing databases; research and statistical uses; government affordability controls.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a coordinating algorithm is used.

rules.conflict_note: Approved 2026-07-20; effective on the first day of the 12th month after enactment (2027-07-01). Section 6(b) bars conflicting municipal ordinances, which may preempt parts of the Jersey City and Hoboken bans once effective.

rules.title: NJ Fair Chance in Housing Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq.)
rules.requirement: Providers may not ask about criminal records before a conditional offer, except methamphetamine manufacture in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex-offender registration. They must disclose their criminal-screening policy in writing before accepting an application fee. Arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile and sealed records may never be considered. Convictions may be considered only within lookbacks (1st degree 6 years; 2nd/3rd degree 4 years; 4th degree 1 year), except listed serious offenses. Withdrawal of an offer requires an individualized assessment. Ads excluding people with records are barred, as is drug or alcohol testing. DCR enforcement: $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000 penalties.
rules.key_value: No criminal inquiry before conditional offer; lookbacks 6/4/1 years
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers of rental dwelling units in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of no more than four units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a building with 4 or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from enactment on 2021-06-18 (first day of the 7th month).

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination in rental housing, incl. source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent to or discriminate against applicants based on protected characteristics, including race, creed, national origin, sex, gender identity, marital or civil union status, disability, sexual orientation, familial status, and source of lawful income or rent payment (e.g., Section 8 vouchers). Fines up to $10,000 for a first offense, plus damages; complaints to DCR within 180 days or Superior Court within 2 years.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental of real property in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: One unit of an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner- or occupant-occupied one-family home; religious-organization preferences; age-restricted housing (familial status).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; religious ownership; senior housing status.

rules.conflict_note: The DCR brochure is a 2015 revision; later amendments may not be reflected.

rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee cap of $50 (P.L.2025, c.405)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential unit. The cap is CPI-adjusted annually from 2027-01-01. Penalties are up to $500 / $750 / $1,000 per offense, and the overcharge is remitted to the applicant.
rules.key_value: $50 max
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property other than units in one- or two-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Units in one- or two-family dwellings; Real Estate Commission licensees unless they are the landlord.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Licensee exemption.

rules.conflict_note: Approved 2026-01-20; effective the first day of the 4th month after (2026-05-01). The older DCA Truth-in-Renting guide says no specific state fee cap exists; it predates this law.

rules.title: NJ Rent Security Deposit Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 et seq.)
rules.requirement: Deposits are capped at 1.5 months' rent, and yearly increases at 10% of the current deposit. Deposits must be held in trust in an insured NJ interest-bearing account, with written notice within 30 days and annually; interest belongs to the tenant. The deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, must be returned within 30 days of termination (5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation; 15 business days after a Safe Housing Act domestic-violence termination). Wrongful withholding carries double damages plus fees; misuse is a disorderly-persons offense.
rules.key_value: Max 1.5 months' rent; 30-day return; double damages
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals in New Jersey, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in by written request; seasonal rentals of 125 days or less (§ 46:8-19).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy and tenant opt-in; seasonal rental status.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq.)
rules.requirement: Residential landlords may not evict or refuse to renew a lease, written or oral, without one of the statutory good causes (2A:18-61.1(a)-(r)), with Notice to Cease and Notice to Quit as required. Illegal-occupancy evictions require relocation of 6 months' rent. Owners evicting for personal occupancy must occupy the unit for at least 6 months, or face treble damages. Civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; 6x rent relocation for illegal occupancy
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including single-family homes, apartments, mobile homes and rooming houses.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or three units and no more than two rental units; transient or seasonal hotel guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a 2-3 unit building; transient status.

rules.title: NJ ban on unconscionable rent increases and mid-lease increases
rules.requirement: Landlords may not raise rent mid-lease. Increases require a proper notice to quit and notice of increase. Tenants cannot be evicted for nonpaid increases that are unconscionable or that violate municipal rent control. In condo or co-op conversions, rents may not be raised to cover conversion costs (2A:18-61.31).
rules.key_value: No numeric cap; unconscionability standard
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with 2-3 units (Anti-Eviction Act exemptions).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unconscionability is decided by a court; owner occupancy.

rules.conflict_note: NJ has no statewide rent control; municipal rent control ordinances apply in addition.

rules.title: NJ 30-year exemption of new multiple dwellings from local rent control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.key_value: 30-year exemption from local rent control
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings within 30 years of completion.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The 30-year window runs from completion; 'newly constructed' qualification under the statute.

rules.conflict_note: State preemption that removes qualifying new buildings from municipal rent control (e.g., Jersey City ch. 260) for 30 years.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination (Code § 218-12)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services (e.g., RealPage) that rely on nonpublic competitor data to set rents. Enforced publicly and privately, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.key_value: Fines up to $2,000/day
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Jersey City.
rules.exemptions: Real estate agents reportedly excluded.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where such services are used.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date known only to the month (secondary source). The NJ FAIR Act § 6(b), effective 2027-07-01, bars conflicting municipal ordinances, so this ban may be partly preempted.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260)
rules.requirement: Rent increases on covered properties are limited under the Rent Control Ordinance (a CPI-referenced cap; amount not stated in the corpus). Increases above the allowed amount require a landlord application, such as capital improvement, vacancy capital improvement or hardship.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties with 5 or more units in Jersey City, unless otherwise exempt.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties; other exemptions by approved Rent Control Exemption Request.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Other ordinance exemptions via Exemption Request; state 30-year new-construction exemption.

rules.conflict_note: New multiple dwellings are exempt for 30 years under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5. The CPI cap formula is not given.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on algorithmic rent coordination (City Code ch. 158)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Hoboken.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where such tools are used.

rules.conflict_note: Secondary source only; citation possibly ch. 158 Art. II. The NJ FAIR Act § 6(b), effective 2027-07-01, may preempt conflicting provisions.

rules.title: Massachusetts statewide rent control initiative (IP 25-21), struck from Nov. 2026 ballot
rules.requirement: Would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. In Cella v. Attorney General (SJC, June 23, 2026), the SJC barred it from the ballot because of its religious exemption. NOT LAW: no statewide rent cap exists, and c. 40P still bars local rent control.
rules.key_value: Proposed lesser of CPI or 5% (not in effect)
rules.coverage_conditions: Proposed: most residential units statewide.
rules.exemptions: Proposed: owner-occupied buildings of 4 or fewer units; units under 10 years old; certain regulated units; short-term rentals; religious, educational or nonprofit facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Proposed exemptions only.

rules.citation: Mass. Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (2026)
rules.conflict_note: Ruling date is given as June 23 in the post and WBUR, and June 24 in a sidebar. The legislature did not pass a compromise bill. A 2028 re-filing is possible.

rules.title: H.5222 (194th) – preventing algorithmic rent fixing
rules.requirement: A pending bill that would restrict algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market. Reported favorably 3/12/2026 as a new draft of H1564 and referred to House Ways and Means. Not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Proposed statewide rental housing; scope not stated.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text not in corpus.

rules.title: S.2983 (194th) – prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: A pending Senate bill that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. A new draft of S.994 and S.1016, it was reported 3/12/2026 and referred to Senate Ways and Means. Not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Proposed statewide rental housing; scope not stated.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text not in corpus.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement: The deposit may not exceed one month's rent. A statement of condition is due at receipt or within 10 days of the tenancy start. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, with a receipt within 30 days. Interest is due yearly at 5% or the lesser bank rate (also on prepaid last month's rent). The deposit must be returned within 30 days of the tenancy's end, with deductions only for unpaid rent or water, tax escalation, and damage itemized under oath. On sale of the property the deposit transfers to the successor, who must notify the tenant within 45 days. An optional fee in lieu of deposit, capped at one month's rent, is authorized under EOHLC regulations. Violations forfeit the deposit and carry treble damages plus 5% interest and fees.
rules.key_value: Max 1 month's rent; 5% interest; 30-day return
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Vacation rental exemption; fee-in-lieu availability depends on EOHLC regulations.

rules.conflict_note: Clause (1)(b) was amended by St. 2025, c. 9, effective 2025-08-01, to also bind lessor's agents.

rules.title: Massachusetts ban on application and other upfront fees (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or the lessor's agent may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month, and the cost of a new lock and key. Application, pet, cleaning and similar fees are prohibited. Conflicting lease terms are void, and treble damages have been awarded (Perry v. Equity Residential).
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security, lock; no application fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Licensed brokers' fees under 254 CMR 7.00; vacation rentals of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether a fee is charged by a licensed broker; third-party screening fees are unsettled.

rules.citation: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9
rules.conflict_note: The limit has been in effect since the 1970s. Its extension to lessors' agents took effect 2025-08-01. The statute does not name application fees expressly.

rules.title: Massachusetts rental broker fee paid only by the party who hired the broker
rules.requirement: A broker fee may be paid only by the party (landlord or tenant) who engaged the broker, so tenants cannot be charged for a landlord-hired broker. Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees, and they must give a signed written fee disclosure at the first meeting (254 CMR 7.00).
rules.key_value: Fee paid only by the engaging party
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental transactions using a licensed broker or salesperson in Massachusetts.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Which party engaged the broker.

rules.conflict_note: Classified under fees as the closest category.

rules.title: Massachusetts housing discrimination law incl. public assistance and children (M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4)
rules.requirement: Owners and agents may not refuse to rent to, discriminate against, or make inquiries or records about applicants based on race, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, veteran status or handicap. They may not discriminate against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies such as vouchers, or because of program requirements. They may not refuse to rent because children will occupy the unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, contiguously located and other covered housing; § 4(10) applies to anyone furnishing rental accommodations.
rules.exemptions: Leasing one unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; for children, also 3-or-fewer-unit dwellings with an elderly or infirm occupant and temporary leasing of the owner's residence; age exemptions for minors and elderly housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy; elderly occupant; c.151B § 1 definitions.

rules.title: Massachusetts anti-retaliation and nonpayment eviction notice protections (M.G.L. c. 186, §§ 18, 11, 31)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not retaliate against tenants for protected activity. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or term change within 6 months of protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal, with damages of 1-3 months' rent or actual damages. Nonpayment terminations under a written lease require a 14-day notice to quit, and the tenant may cure by the answer date (§ 11). Nonpayment notices to quit must include the state tenant-rights form, or courts will not accept the filing (§ 31).
rules.key_value: 6-month retaliation presumption; 14-day nonpayment notice with right to cure
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenants in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Nonpayment notices are excluded from the retaliation presumption.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Protected activity within 6 months; written lease for § 11.

rules.conflict_note: Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction requirement; these are retaliation and notice protections, placed under the closest category.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND/BPDA-funded and inclusionary housing)
rules.requirement: Covered providers may not use blanket criminal bans and must assess applicants case by case. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed, expunged or juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old. Credit scores may not be used to approve or deny; credit history may be used only in place of missing rental history, and lack of credit is not grounds for rejection.
rules.key_value: No convictions older than 5 years; no credit scores
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing receiving Boston DND funding or land, or income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Direct relationship or substantial safety risk; current criminal behavior; conflicting federal or state requirements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted units.

rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.conflict_note: An administrative policy applied through funding and IDP agreements, not a general ordinance. Current status is not confirmed after 2017.

rules.title: Boston fair housing law incl. rental assistance and military status
rules.requirement: Discrimination in renting is barred in Boston based on race, color, religion, disability, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, marital status, rental assistance (e.g., Section 8), family status and military status. Enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any housing rented in the City of Boston.
rules.citation: City of Boston fair housing ordinance (section not stated)
rules.conflict_note: Summary page; no code section, exemptions or effective date.

rules.title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: Landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy must give a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with every notice to quit or non-renewal, and file the notice with the City online. ISD enforcement: a warning for the first offense, then $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction. The requirement cannot be waived by lease.
rules.key_value: Notice with every notice to quit; $300/day after first offense
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners in Boston ending a tenancy or occupancy.
rules.exemptions: Hospitals, skilled nursing and health facilities; nonprofit short-term substance-abuse treatment facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when a tenancy is being ended.

rules.citation: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (Oct. 2020); penalties Sec. 10-11.7
rules.conflict_note: A notice requirement, not a just-cause standard (Boston has no just-cause law). Sec. 10-11.7 may be the penalty section only.

rules.title: Boston rent stabilization home rule petition (H.3744, 193rd)
rules.requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement rent stabilization. Sent to a study order (H5035) on 9/9/2024; the session ended without enactment. NOT LAW.
rules.coverage_conditions: Proposed: Boston residential rentals.
rules.conflict_note: M.G.L. c. 40P bars local rent control without state authorization.

rules.title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744, 193rd)
rules.requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement tenant eviction protections. Sent to a study order on 9/9/2024 and not enacted. NOT LAW.
rules.coverage_conditions: Proposed: Boston residential tenants.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance incl. source of income (ch. 14.04)
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents may not discriminate in showing or renting units, or in tenancy terms, based on protected categories including source of income (Section 8, public benefits). Any reasonable selection standard is allowed if applied uniformly. The Commission may impose fines up to $300 per violation, file criminal complaints and seek injunctions.
rules.key_value: Source of income protected
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing in Cambridge.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family dwellings.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of a two-family dwelling.

rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated.
